title: The Architecture of Complexity
venue: Proceedings of the American Philosophical Society
relevance: Hierarchy, stable intermediate structures and near-decomposability; foundational framing, not an empirical universal law.

authors: Hartwell, Leland H. and Hopfield, John J. and Leibler, Stanislas and Murray, Andrew W.
title: From molecular to modular cell biology
relevance: Functional molecular modules; does not establish that cells have perfectly isolated software-like interfaces.

title: Network motifs: theory and experimental approaches
relevance: Regulatory motifs and their dynamical functions. Persistence detection requires the appropriate regulatory logic and kinetics.

title: Bow ties, metabolism and disease
relevance: Shared cores connect diverse inputs and outputs, with robustness and fragility trade-offs.

title: The theory of facilitated variation
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
relevance: Conserved core processes, flexible regulation, compartmentation and exploratory behaviour. Recipe recomposition illustrates only a small part of this theory.

authors: Prabhakar, Balaji and Dektar, Katherine N. and Gordon, Deborah M.
title: The Regulation of Ant Colony Foraging Activity without Spatial Information
relevance: Local encounters regulate harvester-ant departures. These ants do not need pheromone trails to locate their scattered seeds.

authors: Stouffer, Daniel B. and Bascompte, Jordi
title: Compartmentalization increases food-web persistence
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
relevance: Evidence for compartment effects within the studied food-web models, not a universal guarantee of ecosystem or software stability.

authors: West, Stuart A. and Fisher, Roberta M. and Gardner, Andy and Kiers, E. Toby
title: Major evolutionary transitions in individuality
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
relevance: Cooperation, specialisation and conflict reduction in transitions to higher-level individuals; background rather than an implemented algorithm.

title: Spontaneous evolution of modularity and network motifs
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
relevance: Modularly varying goals can favour modular networks in the studied models. No evolutionary search is implemented in this repository.

authors: Edelman, Gerald M. and Gally, Joseph A.
title: Degeneracy and complexity in biological systems
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
relevance: Structurally different elements can share functions while retaining distinct capabilities. Motivates diverse fallbacks.

authors: Csete, Marie E. and Doyle, John C.
title: Reverse engineering of biological complexity
relevance: Connects modularity, protocol hierarchies, feedback, robustness and cascading fragility.

authors: Abelson, Harold and Allen, Don and Coore, Daniel and Hanson, Chris and Homsy, George and Knight, Thomas F. and Nagpal, Radhika and Rauch, Erik and Sussman, Gerald Jay and Weiss, Ron
title: Amorphous computing
relevance: Biologically inspired coordination of many unreliable, locally connected computational elements.

title: Biological robustness
relevance: Robustness through control, alternative mechanisms, modularity and decoupling; useful background across the catalogue.

title: The Evolution of the Algorithms for Collective Behavior
relevance: Local interaction rules depend on environmental conditions, resource distribution and operating costs.

authors: Yi, Tau-Mu and Huang, Yun and Simon, Melvin I. and Doyle, John
title: Robust perfect adaptation in bacterial chemotaxis through integral feedback control
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
evidence: Control-theoretic analysis of a biological mechanism
relevance: Integral feedback explains robust adaptation under specified conditions. Our service controller is not a biochemical simulation.

authors: Waters, Christopher M. and Bassler, Bonnie L.
title: Quorum sensing: cell-to-cell communication in bacteria
venue: Annual Review of Cell and Developmental Biology
relevance: Chemical communication and collective regulation. Signal concentration also depends on transport and loss, not just cell count.

title: Kinetic Proofreading: A New Mechanism for Reducing Errors in Biosynthetic Processes Requiring High Specificity
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
relevance: Candidate for a future pattern on repeated discrimination with energy and time costs. Ordinary repeated validation is not equivalent to kinetic proofreading.

authors: Toda, Satoshi and Blauch, Lucas R. and Tang, Sindy K. Y. and Morsut, Leonardo and Lim, Wendell A.
title: Programming self-organizing multicellular structures with synthetic cell-cell signaling
relevance: Engineered cell signalling and adhesion yield self-organising structures. These are engineered biological systems, not direct evidence for their evolutionary origin.

title: Amorphous Computing project home page
relevance: Original project context, demonstrations and links. Accessed 2026-10-13; no publication year asserted for the web page.
